Interactive D3 scatterplot matrix

pv_pairs.Rd

All pairwise relationships in a set of numeric columns, drawn as one matrix: scatter cells below the diagonal, each variable's own histogram on it, and the correlation coefficient for every pair above it, printed large and inked by sign and strength on the diverging ramp - a strong positive and a strong negative pair announce themselves before any single cell is read. The correlation method's name appears once, under the chart's heading, never per cell.

Usage

pv_pairs(
  data,
  columns = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  method = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall"),
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  mode = "auto",
  duration = 400,
  source = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  elementId = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

columns

Character vector of numeric column names to pair, in matrix order. NULL (the default) takes the first 6 numeric columns (excluding any mapped to color or label). At most 8 - past that the cells shrink below anything readable.

color

Optional name of a grouping column, coloured from the categorical palette — at most as many levels as the active theme's palette has colours (8 in the packaged theme). Rows with a missing group are dropped with a warning.

label

Optional name of a column naming each row, shown first in scatter-cell tooltips.

method

Which correlation the upper triangle shows: "pearson" (default), "spearman", or "kendall", computed by stats::cor() on pairwise-complete observations.

title, subtitle

Optional chart heading text.

mode

"auto" (default: follow the viewer's light/dark setting), "light", or "dark".

duration

Entrance transition length in ms.

source

Optional source/credit line, shown small and grey at the bottom left — e.g. "Source: Bundesamt für Statistik".

width, height, elementId

Standard htmlwidgets sizing arguments.

Value

An htmlwidget.

Details

Variable names label the diagonal cells, and axis ticks appear only on the matrix's outer edge - the left column and the bottom row - so the inner cells stay clean. Hovering a scatter point names the pair of variables (and the row, when label is mapped); hovering a correlation cell restates the coefficient to three decimals with the number of pairs behind it.

Missing values follow the pairwise rule: correlations use pairwise-complete observations, and each scatter cell drops only the rows incomplete for its own pair, so no cell loses data to a gap in some other column. Rows with any missing value are counted in a single warning. A column that is constant in the data has no defined correlations — those cells show an em dash, and a warning names the column.

Examples

pv_pairs(subset(pv_fiscal, year == 2025),
         columns = c("resource_per_capita", "resource_index",
                     "equalization_chf"),
         title = "How Lucerne's fiscal measures move together")
